structure: Part 10, Upload documents. Mined all 10 traces in full (every action list read, snapshots and network logs taken): 7 from documents.fit.spec.js (renders the upload guidance and document fields; save and add another with nothing entered names every field; a date of issue that is not a real date; continuing with a document type chosen but the rest blank is held on the page; documents are optional: continuing with nothing chosen moves on; a complete document is listed with its virus check status, and removed after a confirmation page; upload documents from the hub: save and return to overview from the hub) and 3 from snagging.fit.spec.js (S28 date of issue picker, with a no-JavaScript context; S29 before any document is added; S31 the table after upload and add another, two documents, with a no-JavaScript context). Both spec files were read as well. Every trace reaches the page through the opening run (create-notification as live-animals, origin of the import France, what are you importing cattle), which other parts own. Pages in this slice, in order: (1) /design-release-2.1/upload-documents, title 'Upload documents - Import notification service - GOV.UK', reached by direct navigation or from the notification hub's 'Upload documents' task link (?from=hub). Layout: notification status banner (Draft tag and 'Live animals - <reference>'), caption 'Documents', h1 'Upload documents', intro paragraph, 'Other documents you may need to attach include:' list, a details component 'Check which additional documents you must upload' holding a table and a GOV.UK link, then a 'File upload' card (Document reference, Document type select of 14 options, Date of issue with MOJ date picker, Attachment with requirements list and a drop zone), 'Save and add another' inside the card, a table of saved documents inside the card once one is added, then Save and continue, Save and return to overview, and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link. States seen: empty (no table), file chosen (drop zone shows the file name), one and two documents added, each error state (nothing entered, not a real date, type chosen with the rest blank), and no-JavaScript renders. (2) /design-release-2.1/upload-documents/<id>/delete, title 'Delete this document? - Import notification service - GOV.UK', a confirmation page with inset text, a summary list of the document, warning button 'Yes, delete' and a 'No, cancel' link; conditional on a document having been added. Network: every submit is a form-urlencoded POST to /design-release-2.1/upload-documents carrying only the file name, not the file; a simulated virus check posts to the unprefixed /upload-documents/virus-check/<id> and returns {"virusStatus":null}, so the status never moves on from 'Scanning for virus'. Not reached by any trace in this part: clicking 'Save and return to overview', clicking 'Cancel and return to overview', opening the details component, any file rule error, a date in the future, a germinal-products notification, and a completed virus check.

claims.statement: The Upload documents page is at /design-release-2.1/upload-documents and its browser title is 'Upload documents - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
claims.quote: Upload documents - Import notification service - GOV.UK

claims.statement: The page heading is 'Upload documents', with the caption 'Documents' above it.

The caption and heading use custom classes (app-upload-documents-page__caption, app-upload-documents-page__heading) rather than govuk-caption-l and govuk-heading-l; a standard GOV.UK caption and heading could replace them.
Above the caption the page shows the notification status: a 'Draft' tag and the text 'Live animals - ' followed by the notification reference.
claims.note: Rendered with custom classes app-dr2-notification-status and a govuk-tag with app-dr2-review-status__tag--draft.

claims.statement: The page opens with an intro paragraph about the health certificate, when to upload, and language and completeness of documents.
claims.quote: You must attach an health certificate if this consignment requires one. If you do not have it now, you can add it later. All documents should be uploaded before the consignment arrives at the UK port. Documents must be in English and you must upload all pages.

claims.statement: The page lists other documents the user may need to attach, as a bulleted list: import licences or authorisations, and commercial documents or invoices.
claims.quote:
Other documents you may need to attach include:

import licences or authorisations
commercial documents or invoices

claims.statement: A details component titled 'Check which additional documents you must upload' sits below the list.
claims.quote: Check which additional documents you must upload

claims.statement: Inside the details component is a table with columns 'Consignment' and 'Documents needed' and three rows: animals that do not need a health certificate need the exporter's declaration that they are fit to travel; livestock transiting bluetongue restricted territories need Bluetongue declaration GBHC172; rodents imported for research purposes need an RM39 licence and supplementary health certificate.
claims.quote: Consignment | Documents needed | Animals that do not need a health certificate | Exporter's declaration that they are fit to travel | Livestock transiting bluetongue restricted territories | Bluetongue declaration GBHC172 | Rodents imported for research purposes | RM39 licence and supplementary health certificate
claims.note: Quote joins the table cells with ' | '. The details component was never opened in a trace; the content is in the DOM.

claims.statement: The details component ends with a link 'Check the documents you need' to the GOV.UK guidance page import-of-products-animals-food-and-feed-system, opening in a new tab, followed by 'on GOV.UK (opens in a new tab).'
claims.quote: Check the documents you need on GOV.UK (opens in a new tab).
claims.note: The href carries a Google Analytics _gl tracking parameter, shortened here to '...'. The link text and the '(opens in a new tab)' sit partly outside the link.

claims.statement: The document fields sit in a custom card section headed 'File upload' (an h2), built from app-upload-documents-card classes rather than a GOV.UK component.
The first field in the card is a text input labelled 'Document reference' (name documentReference), with no hint.
The second field is a select labelled 'Document type' (name documentType), defaulting to 'Select one'.

The Document type select offers 13 types after 'Select one', in this order: Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate (ITAHC), Veterinary health certificate, Air waybill, Import permit, Letter of authority (Directive 2008/61/EC), Commercial invoice, Sea waybill, Rail waybill, Bill of lading, Catch certificate, Laboratory sampling results for aflatoxin (Reg 2019/1793), Journey log, Other.

The list is the prototype's hard-coded fixture.

claims.statement: The same Document type list is shown for a live-animals notification of cattle; the traces never show whether it changes by commodity or notification type.
The third field is a text input labelled 'Date of issue' (name dateOfIssue) with the hint 'For example, 27/3/2026', a single field rather than a GOV.UK date input with day, month and year.
claims.quote: For example, 27/3/2026

claims.statement: The Date of issue field uses the Ministry of Justice date picker component (moj-datepicker, data-module moj-date-picker), whose toggle button has the hidden label 'Choose date'.
claims.note: MOJ Frontend is one of the accepted government libraries the programme goal names.

claims.statement: Clicking the date picker toggle opens a calendar dialog showing the current month ('November 2026'), with the toggle's aria-expanded set to true and today's date (27 November 2026) marked as current and selected.
claims.quote: hidden=false | title=November 2026 | expanded=true | current=<button type="button" data-testid="27/11/2026" style="display: block;" class="moj-datepicker__button moj-datepicker__calendar-day moj-datepicker__button--selected moj-datepicker__button--current

claims.statement: The calendar dialog has Previous year, Previous month, Next month and Next year buttons, a Monday-first week grid, and 'Select' and 'Close' buttons.
claims.quote: buttons=Select,Close | nav=Previous year,Previous month,Next month,Next year,Monday 26 October 2026

claims.statement: The date picker sets no minimum or maximum date and disables no day, so a future date of issue can be picked.
claims.note: Inferred from the absence of min/max data attributes and disabled buttons; no trace submits a future date, so whether the server refuses one is not shown.

claims.statement: Without JavaScript the Date of issue field is a plain text input with its label and hint, and no date picker toggle is shown.
claims.quote:
govuk-template__body | toggle=0 | dateField=Date of issue
For example, 27/3/2026

claims.statement: The fourth field is a file input labelled 'Attachment' (name attachment), with the hint 'Your file must be:' followed by a bulleted list of file rules.
claims.quote: Your file must be:
claims.note: The spec file calls this section 'File upload'; the field's own label is 'Attachment'.

claims.statement: The file rules shown are: files that are smaller than 50MB; PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, JPG, PNG, XLS or XLSX; up to a maximum of 15 files; ZIP files are not allowed for security reasons.
claims.quote:
files that are smaller than 50MB
PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, JPG, PNG, XLS or XLSX
up to a maximum of 15 files
ZIP files are not allowed for security reasons

claims.statement: No trace drives a file that breaks a stated rule (over 50MB, a disallowed type, a ZIP, or more than 15 files), so the errors for those cases, and whether they are enforced, are not shown.
The file is chosen through a custom drop zone (app-file-upload module) showing 'No file chosen', a 'Choose file' label and the text 'or drop file', rather than the GOV.UK file upload component.
claims.quote:
No file chosen
or drop file
claims.note: GOV.UK Frontend's file upload component has a drop zone enhancement that could replace it. The 'or drop file' text is still shown with JavaScript off (S28 action 51); drag and drop is never driven.

claims.statement: Once a file is chosen, the drop zone status changes from 'No file chosen' to the file's name (for example 'itahc.pdf') and the hidden field attachmentFileName takes that name.
The card ends with a 'Save and add another' button (action add-another) below the fields.
Below the card the page has a 'Save and continue' primary button, a 'Save and return to overview' secondary button and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link to the notification hub.

claims.statement: The page's Back link goes to the notification hub (/design-release-2.1/notification-hub), whether or not the page was opened from the hub.

claims.statement: Documents are optional: choosing Save and continue with nothing entered moves on to the roles and addresses page (/design-release-2.1/roles-and-addresses).
In the linear journey, the page after Upload documents is the roles and addresses page.

Save and add another with nothing entered keeps the user on the page and shows an error summary titled 'There is a problem' listing, in order: 'Enter a document reference', 'Select a document type', 'Enter a date of issue', 'Upload a document'.
claims.quote:
There is a problem
Enter a document reference
Select a document type
Enter a date of issue
Upload a document

claims.statement: A missing document reference shows 'Enter a document reference', linked from the summary to #document-reference and shown inline above the input.
No document type shows 'Select a document type', linked from the summary to #document-type and shown inline above the select.
A missing date of issue shows 'Enter a date of issue', linked from the summary to #date-of-issue and shown inline.
No file chosen shows 'Upload a document', linked from the summary to #attachment, shown inline in the Attachment field, and the drop zone takes an error style.
claims.note: The field gets app-upload-documents-card__field--error and the drop zone app-upload-documents-card__dropzone--error, custom error classes.

claims.statement: Each inline error message carries the visually hidden prefix 'Error:' and the input or select takes the GOV.UK error style.
claims.quote:
govuk-error-message :: document-reference-error :: Error:
Enter a document reference

claims.statement: When the page shows errors, its browser title stays 'Upload documents - Import notification service - GOV.UK' with no 'Error:' prefix.
claims.quote:
Upload documents - Import notification service - GOV.UK
##There is a problem
claims.note: GOV.UK guidance adds 'Error: ' to the title when a page has errors; the prototype does not.

claims.statement: A failed submit re-renders the page in the POST response (200) rather than redirecting.
A date of issue that is not a real date (30/2/2026) shows 'Enter a real date', linked to #date-of-issue, alongside 'Upload a document' when no file is chosen.

Enter a real date

###date-of-issue=Enter a real date | #attachment=Upload a document

claims.statement: On an error, the values already entered (reference, type and date) are kept in the fields.

Once a document type is chosen, every other document field is required: choosing Save and continue with only the type (Air waybill) set holds the user on the page with 'Enter a document reference', 'Enter a date of issue' and 'Upload a document'.
claims.quote:
There is a problem
Enter a document reference
Enter a date of issue
Upload a document

claims.statement: No trace shows the errors when only a reference, a date or a file is entered with no type, so whether entering any one field (not only the type) makes the others required is not shown.
No trace submits a date in the future, a date with a missing part or text that is not a date in the d/m/yyyy shape, so any other date error message is not shown.
No trace shows a length limit or character rule on the document reference.
Save and add another with every field complete saves the document, redirects back to the Upload documents page, and clears the fields for the next document.

Saved documents are listed in a table inside the File upload card, below the Save and add another button, with column headings 'Document reference', 'Document type', 'Date of issue', 'Status' and a visually hidden 'Action'.
claims.quote: Document reference Document type Date of issue Status Action
claims.note: A GOV.UK table with the extra class app-upload-documents-table and equal-width custom col classes.

claims.statement: Each row shows the reference entered, the document type's label (not its value), and the date of issue as entered, for example 'ITAHC-001', 'Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate (ITAHC)', '25/11/2026'.
claims.quote: ITAHC-001 Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate (ITAHC) 25/11/2026

claims.statement: The table does not show the file name; the file name is shown only on the delete confirmation page.
claims.quote:
Document reference	Document type	Date of issue	Status	
Action
claims.note: Inferred from the column headings and row cells, which carry no file name.

claims.statement: Each saved document's Status cell shows a blue tag 'Scanning for virus', preceded by visually hidden text 'Virus check status for <reference>'.
claims.quote: Virus check status for ITAHC-001 Scanning for virus

claims.statement: The page runs a simulated virus check in the browser: about 2.5 seconds after a document is listed it posts to /upload-documents/virus-check/<document id> and gets back JSON with a virusStatus.
claims.note: The script is upload-documents-virus-check.js. The call needs JavaScript; it is a stand-in for a real virus-scanning service.

claims.statement: Under Design Release 2.1 the virus check call returns {"virusStatus":null}, so the tag stays 'Scanning for virus' and never moves on, even after 4 seconds.
claims.note: The spec file explains the route is unprefixed and reads the root (DR1) session. This is a prototype defect, not a design.

claims.statement: The statuses a document reaches after its virus check (for example clean or infected), and their tags and wording, are never shown.
Without JavaScript a saved document's tag still reads 'Scanning for virus', since nothing checks its status.
claims.quote: ITAHC-001 | Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate (ITAHC) | 25/11/2026 | Virus check status for ITAHC-001 / Scanning for virus | Remove /  ITAHC-001

claims.statement: Each row has a 'Remove' link, with the visually hidden reference after it, going to /design-release-2.1/upload-documents/<document id>/delete.
Adding a second document (Air waybill, AWB-002) adds a second row below the first, so documents are listed in the order they were added.
claims.quote:
ITAHC-001 | Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate (ITAHC) | 25/11/2026 | Virus check status for ITAHC-001 / Scanning for virus | Remove /  ITAHC-001
AWB-002 | Air waybill | 25/11/2026 | Virus check status for AWB-002 / Scanning for virus | Remove /  AWB-002

claims.statement: The saved documents persist in the session: a fresh no-JavaScript page on the same session shows both documents.
The form posts as application/x-www-form-urlencoded and sends only the chosen file's name (attachment and attachmentFileName), not the file's content, so no file is uploaded anywhere.
claims.note: A real service needs a file upload and storage integration the prototype cannot express.

claims.statement: No upload to a storage or virus-scanning service is seen in any trace; the real file upload integration is not shown.
The 'up to a maximum of 15 files' rule is never driven; no trace shows what happens when a 16th document is added, or whether the page hides the card when the limit is reached.

Clicking Remove opens a confirmation page at /design-release-2.1/upload-documents/<document id>/delete with the title 'Delete this document? - Import notification service - GOV.UK' and the heading 'Delete this document?'.
claims.quote: Delete this document? - Import notification service - GOV.UK

claims.statement: The delete page shows inset text 'This will remove the document from this notification.'
claims.quote: This will remove the document from this notification.

claims.statement: The delete page shows a summary list of the document with keys 'Document reference', 'Document type', 'Date of issue' and 'File', and the values as entered, with the type's label and the file name (for example itahc.pdf); the rows have no change links.
claims.quote:
Document reference	ITAHC-001
Document type	Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate (ITAHC)
Date of issue	25/11/2026
File	itahc.pdf

claims.statement: The delete page says 'This action cannot be undone.' below the summary list.
The delete page has a red warning button 'Yes, delete' and a 'No, cancel' link back to /design-release-2.1/upload-documents, in a button group.
claims.quote: No, cancel

claims.statement: The delete page's Back link goes to the Upload documents page.

The delete page is built only from GOV.UK components (heading-l, inset text, summary list, body, button group, warning button) in a two-thirds column, with no caption and no notification status banner.
Choosing 'No, cancel' returns to the Upload documents page with the document still listed.
Choosing 'Yes, delete' posts to the delete URL, redirects to the Upload documents page and removes the document; with none left, the table is no longer shown.
After a document is deleted, the Upload documents page shows no success or notification banner.
The notification hub has an 'Upload documents' task link, with status 'To do' before any document is added, going to /design-release-2.1/upload-documents?from=hub.
When opened from the hub, the page carries a hidden field from=hub and posts to /design-release-2.1/upload-documents?from=hub.
When opened from the hub, Save and continue with nothing entered returns to the notification hub instead of moving on to roles and addresses.
claims.note: The test is titled 'save and return to overview from the hub' but clicks the 'Save and continue' button (action continue), not 'Save and return to overview'.

claims.statement: No trace clicks 'Save and return to overview' (action hub) or the 'Cancel and return to overview' link, so where they go and whether Cancel discards entered fields is not shown.
No trace shows the hub task status for Upload documents after a document is added.
No trace shows Save and continue with a complete document entered but not yet added, so whether that saves the document before moving on is not shown.
Every trace walks a live-animals notification; the Upload documents page for a germinal-products notification, and its guidance text, are not shown.

The Upload documents page uses custom page and card classes for its layout (app-upload-documents-page__intro, __content, __body, __list, __details, app-upload-documents-card__field, __form-group, __label, __input, __select, __hint, __requirements, __add-button, __saved) and the shared form action classes app-origin-form-actions and app-origin-actions; the fields themselves are GOV.UK label, input, select, hint, list, details and table.
The page's fields and buttons all render and submit without JavaScript: the no-JavaScript render has the reference, type, date and file inputs and all three submit buttons.
claims.quote: inputs=text:documentReference,select-one:documentType,text:dateOfIssue,file:attachment,hidden:attachmentFileName | buttons=Save and add another,Save and continue,Save and return to overview

claims.statement: The date hint example '27/3/2026' shows a day and month without leading zeros, so the field expects dates in d/m/yyyy form.
claims.note: Inferred from the hint and from the values the tests fill (30/2/2026, 25/11/2026); whether a leading zero or another separator is accepted is not shown.
